Note · Goldman Sachs mission & forces — the purpose statement followed the strategy: societal while Goldman diversified, "exceptional" and 1979 heritage once it retreated to banking and asset management. The force that binds hardest is the regulator's capital rule, and the dealer's moat moved from flow to financing

Strategy / environment-scan note · Maps to Course 04 (Competitive Strategy: five forces from a dealer's seat: venues, non-bank liquidity, private credit, Big Tech, regulators), Course 11 (Global Strategy, Macro & Responsible Business: the rise and fade of sustainability and D&I language), E6 (Crisis Leadership & Resilience: COVID, 2022, SVB, tariffs, the 2026 private-credit stress), E9 (Geopolitics & Macro: tariffs, Iran, US–China, fiscal deficits), E12 (Culture as Strategy: four core values, the Business Principles, 1MDB) · Written 2026-10-25 · Companion to goldman hub and goldman strategy financials; counterpart to tradeweb mission forces

  • Source: _ingest/raw/goldman/articles.jsonl (262 items, 2019–Oct 2026). I read all 7 shareholder letters (FY2019–FY2025; each dated to fiscal year-end but published ~Mar–Apr of the next year), both Investor Day sets (2020 consolidated; 2023, eight decks), the 32 earnings releases, the forward-looking statements in the IR stubs, and the leader podcasts. I pulled the "About Goldman Sachs" boilerplate from all 38 releases that carry it and counted theme terms in each letter by script (counts derived). The Purpose & Values web page scraped empty, so mission language comes from letters, decks, releases and podcasts. No 10-K, proxy or earnings-call Q&A was used. Everything is Goldman's own channel: a record of what the firm wants said, read here for what it reveals and omits. Financial series come from the releases via reader notes A and B and are marked (derived) where I computed them.
  • Core claim: Goldman's stated purpose changed four times in seven years, and each change tracked the strategy. A societal mission ("advance sustainable economic growth and financial opportunity", FY2019–20) arrived with the push to diversify into consumer and transaction banking. It vanished in FY2021 behind a returns slogan. In FY2022 it became an aspiration to be "the world’s most exceptional financial institution", just as Solomon narrowed consumer. By FY2025 the values were anchored in John Whitehead's 1979 Business Principles. The legal boilerplate followed the same path: "and consumer banking" entered in mid-2021 and was gone by Apr 17 2023, seven weeks after Investor Day 2023. Climate, inclusion and the One Million Black Women program fell from 13, 3 and 12 mentions to zero in the FY2023–25 letters (derived), with nothing formally retracted. What Goldman actually optimises for is ROE against public targets, client wallet-share rank, and "durable" revenue at low capital intensity. Its tailwinds are volatility, the financing book and the AWM fee build. Its binding constraint is the Fed's stress capital buffer (6.7% → 3.4%). From a dealer's seat the forces are mixed: venues compress spreads, but Goldman moved its growth into balance-sheet financing that venues can't touch. Non-bank market makers and private-credit funds are the rivals that matter, and both are also its clients. Big Tech set the terms of the consumer bet and supplies its engineers. Regulators swung from headwind to tailwind in 2025. Goldman admits cyclicality, consumer losses, capital rules and AI execution risk. Its channels say almost nothing about rival dealers, venue consolidation, or its conflicts as both originator and investor in private credit.

1. Mission and identity

1a. What Goldman says it is for (verbatim, dated)

Date (as dated in corpus) Where Line (verbatim) Read
FY2019 letter (pub. ~Mar 2020) Letter, "Our Purpose and Core Values" "Goldman Sachs’ mission is to advance sustainable economic growth and financial opportunity across the globe." Societal purpose, launched with the diversification plan
Jan 29 2020 Investor Day release (Solomon) "We are resolute in fulfilling our purpose of putting capital and ideas to work to evolve organizations, accelerate global economies and amplify personal prosperity." A second purpose line in the same month; the deck's own box still reads "We advance sustainable economic growth and financial opportunity"
FY2020 letter Letter "We never lost sight of our purpose: to advance sustainable economic growth and financial opportunity." Purpose as crisis anchor (COVID, 1MDB)
FY2021 letter Letter No purpose box. In its place: "Our Strategy to Produce Higher, More Consistent Returns" Purpose replaced by a returns plan in the record year (ROE 23.0%)
FY2022 letter Letter, "Our Purpose" "We aspire to be the world’s most exceptional financial institution, united by our shared values of partnership, client service, integrity and excellence." Excellence replaces society. Same letter: "In 2022, we decided to significantly narrow our ambitions for our consumer strategy."
FY2023 letter Letter Same purpose box; identity: "There’s no ambiguity about who we are — a preeminent global investment bank" The firm defines itself by what it stopped being
FY2024 letter Letter No purpose statement; core values and Business Principles only Purpose goes silent
FY2025 letter Letter "The firm’s core values are drawn from our 14 Business Principles, which were written by John Whitehead in 1979." Heritage replaces aspiration. The principles had been printed in every letter since FY2019; FY2025 is the first to name their author and year
Jan 23 2026 Solomon podcast "we talk about our purpose as an organization is to really be the most exceptional financial services firm in the world." The FY2022 line survives in speech

The arc: 2019–20 serve society and diversify; 2021 produce higher returns; 2022–23 be exceptional, no ambiguity; 2024–25 values from 1979. The societal purpose lived exactly as long as the consumer bank did.

1b. The "About Goldman Sachs" boilerplate, 2019 → 2026

First seen → last seen (corpus) Self-description (verbatim opening) Releases carrying it Read
May 16 2019 → Dec 18 2020 "a leading global investment banking, securities and investment management firm" 16 The pre-Solomon identity, unchanged through the 2020 Investor Day
Jun 21 2021 → Feb 21 2023 "a leading global financial institution that delivers a broad range of financial services across investment banking, securities, investment management and consumer banking" 19 "Consumer banking" and "financial institution" arrive together, at the Marcus/GreenSky peak (GreenSky announced Sep 15 2021)
Apr 17 2023 → Sep 8 2026 "a leading global financial institution that delivers a broad range of financial services to a large and diversified client base" 35 The business list is deleted, not just consumer. First seen on the Visual Structuring expansion release (Apr 17 2023; last old-style use Feb 21 2023), months before the PFM and GreenSky sales

What the boilerplate shows (inference unless noted): 1. The legal self-description changed once to add consumer and once to remove it. The removal came between Feb 21 2023 (last old-style use, the Investor Day notice) and Apr 17 2023 (first new-style use), i.e. right after Investor Day 2023 and alongside the Marcus loan sale, before the GreenSky write-down. 2. "Financial institution" outlived the consumer bank. Goldman kept the broader noun after dropping the business that justified it, and stopped listing its businesses at all. 3. The forward-looking statements in IR stubs are a second, finer clock. They list "strategic alternatives for credit card partnerships and the pending sale of GreenSky" (Dec 2023). The phrase "the opportunities presented by AI" first appears in May 2025 (Bernstein conference stub) (corpus search).

1c. Values and culture claims

  • Four core values, constant since FY2019: partnership, client service, integrity, excellence. The letter says Goldman "distilled our Business Principles into 4 core values". The order changes in speech (Solomon, Jan 2026: client service first).
  • The Business Principles, printed every year, include the line Goldman most needed in 2020: "Our assets are our people, capital and reputation. If any of these is ever diminished, the last is the most difficult to restore."
  • 1MDB as the culture test. Solomon's memo (Oct 22 2020): "Our success as a firm can only be ensured through a culture rooted in integrity, shaped by a long-term mindset". The Board called it "an institutional failure". The fixes were a reputational-risk committee of control-side members "empowered to stop any transaction", and a compliance division that had "nearly doubled in size" since 2012 (as stated). About $174m of compensation was clawed back or cut (goldman one gs culture).
  • People as the factory. Waldron (Jun 5 2025): "It's a people firm. It's a human capital driven firm." Solomon (Sep 8 2026): "We are in a period of rapid technological change, but we know our people are still this firm’s greatest asset."
  • One Goldman Sachs as an operating ethos: a day-one memo (Oct 2018), a repair for a firm that Waldron said had "gotten more Balkanized" (2019), and by 2025 extended to operations. Solomon: "this is a moment for us to expand our One Goldman Sachs ethos to our internal operating model." (FY2025 letter).

1d. The fading of sustainability and D&I

Term counts per shareholder letter (derived by script; case-insensitive):

Letter Words "climate" "inclusion" "Black women" Sustainable-finance target IPO board-diversity policy "AI"
FY2019 4,847 2 2 0 2 1 0
FY2020 6,173 13 3 6 3 1 0
FY2021 4,610 6 2 12 3 2 0
FY2022 4,405 2 0 3 2 0 0
FY2023 3,250 0 0 0 0 0 5
FY2024 3,085 0 0 0 0 0 4
FY2025 4,732 0 0 0 0 0 10
  • At the peak the language was personal: "Advancing diversity and inclusion is a priority of mine" (FY2020). The firm would underwrite US and Western European IPOs only for companies with "at least one diverse board member", raised to two in July 2021. The $750bn ten-year sustainable-finance target (set 2019) was ~55% achieved in three years (FY2022 letter).
  • The last appearance is a "Sustainable Finance" section in the FY2022 letter. From FY2023 the only D&I sentence left is the Business Principle printed at the back: "our people must reflect the diversity of the communities and cultures in which we operate." FY2024 adds that the firm is "proud of the diversity of the partner class of 2024".
  • The number $750 billion returns in FY2025 with a new meaning: "We expect fee-paying alternative assets under supervision to reach $750 billion by the end of 2030."
  • Reading (inference): nothing is retracted. The topics simply stop being reported as strategy once the purpose stops being societal. AI fills the vacated space: zero mentions through FY2022, ten in FY2025. ESG and climate releases were filtered out of this corpus (DIGEST §1), so this shows a fade in the CEO's own voice, not necessarily in activity.

1e. What Goldman actually optimises for (judged by actions; inference)

Stated Revealed by action Evidence
"Advance sustainable economic growth" (2019) ROE against public targets. The first Investor Day set >13% ROE and ~60% efficiency. The 2021 purpose box became a returns plan. The Management Committee moved to 100% performance-based PSUs (FY2022 letter) ROE 10.0% (2019) → 23.0% (2021) → 10.2% (2022) → 7.5% (2023) → 15.0% (2025) → 23.5% (Q2 2026)
Client service Wallet-share rank, not revenue. Waldron: "We kind of obsess over those rankings. We're not obsessing over revenue." (Jun 5 2025) GBM wallet share +390bp (FY2025 letter)
Diversify "Durable" revenue at low capital intensity. The same word justified Folio (2020), GreenSky (2021), Industry Ventures (2025), Innovator and NEOS (2025–26) Management fees $6.1bn (2019) → $11.54bn (2025); principal investments $64bn → ~$6bn
"Capital is a commodity" (Solomon, 2019) Financing is the moat. The balance sheet was put to work in prime, repo and structured lending FICC + Equities financing $7.12bn of $25.67bn markets revenue in 2022 (27.7%) → $11.45bn of $31.06bn in 2025 (36.9%) (derived); Q3 2026 Equities financing $3.37bn > intermediation $3.08bn
Partnership Capital-light at the firm level. Exit consumer and principal investing, cut stress losses, fight the SCB SCB 6.7% → 3.4%; Solomon: "Today’s announcement is a reflection of the work we have done over the years to reduce our capital intensity" (Jul 1 2025)

The tension (inference): the 2020 plan said durability would come from new businesses: transaction banking, consumer, wealth for "everyday Americans". It came instead from the old dealer's balance sheet plus AWM fees. The mission statement didn't drive the strategy. It narrated whichever strategy was working.

A = admitted by Goldman in the corpus. I = my inference.

# Tailwind Evidence (dated, quantified) A / I
T1 Volatility and client activity drive markets revenue Q1 2020 Global Markets return 19.7% vs the 11% Investor Day threshold (Varadhan, Apr 16 2020). Q2 2020 FICC $4.24bn. "It’s true the surge in capital markets activity was a big tailwind." (FY2021 letter). Q2 2026 Equities $7.42bn (+72% YoY) A
T2 Financing as ballast Financing share of markets revenue 19% vs peers' 32% (ID20) → 36.9% (2025) (derived). Waldron: "In the last five years, the standard deviation of our results is 6%. In the prior 10 years, it was 24%." (Jun 5 2025; window and method unstated) A
T3 AWM fee build and the alternatives wave Alts raised $438bn since Investor Day 2020; new goals $75–100bn a year and $750bn fee-paying alts AUS by 2030 (FY2025 letter). AUS record $1.86tn (2019) → ">$4.0 trillion" (Aug 18 2026 release). Deals: T. Rowe, Industry Ventures, Innovator, NEOS, LCN A
T4 Private credit's structural growth; banks' retreat after the GFC Solomon: "we are operating at the fulcrum of one of the most important structural trends in finance today: the emergence and growth of private credit" (FY2024 letter). Capital Solutions Group (Jan 2025); ~$145bn of GS private credit A
T5 Capital relief SCB 6.6% (2020) → 6.4% → 6.3% → 5.5% → 6.2% → 3.4% (2025–26). Dividend $0.85 → $5.00. Fed intent: "a more transparent and fair approach to these tests" (Jul 1 2025) A
T6 M&A / IPO rebound and AI as a fee engine "As the leader in M&A advisory and equity underwriting, a resurgence in activity will undoubtedly be a tailwind for Goldman Sachs." (Oct 17 2023). "Technology and AI-led innovation should be a catalyst for significant capital markets activity in 2026" (Jan 5 2026). AI-related debt ~18% of 2026 IG supply (Research, Aug 5 2026) A
T7 ETFs and passive flow Issuer, AP, market maker and launch platform (ETF Accelerator, >$3bn launched by Jun 2024); Innovator and NEOS make GSAM the #8 active ETF manager (as stated). ETFs reach "40% of the tape at times" in stress (Aug 18 2026) A
T8 US regulatory pivot on digital assets SAB 121 rescinded, GENIUS Act (McDermott, Jun 2025); GS DAP spun out with Tradeweb (Nov 2024); BNY tokenized MMFs (Jul 2025) A
T9 AI as an internal productivity lever "over 12,000 engineers" (Sep 8 2026); GS AI Assistant firmwide (Jan 2025); OneGS 3.0 (2025). Solomon: "if we get this right, I don't think it significantly lowers the number of people we have." (Jan 23 2026) A for the program; I for any margin gain (rivals have the same tools)

Top five (judgement): T2 financing, T3 AWM fees, T5 capital relief, T1 volatility, T4 private credit. T1 should be discounted, not banked. T4 is also the source of headwind H6.

3. Headwinds and challenges

# Headwind Evidence A / I
H1 The failed consumer diversification Marcus loan sale ~$470m loss (Q1 2023); GreenSky goodwill impairment $504m (Q2 2023); "selected items" cut 2023 EPS by $8.04; Apple Card markdowns $2.26bn against a $2.48bn reserve release (Jan 7 2026). Admitted in one letter sentence (FY2022) A, minimally
H2 A capital-markets-heavy mix, so cyclicality "We have a mix of businesses that is very capital markets heavy." (Solomon, Feb 24 2023). Q3 2022 IB revenue −57% (as stated); 2023 M&A at a ten-year low A
H3 Balance-sheet investing drag ~$10bn negative revenue swing in 2022: "The biggest drag was actually the asset management performance of that balance sheet" (Feb 24 2023) A
H4 Capital rules SCB error (Sep 2020); 2024 increase disputed; Basel III endgame: "in our view the proposal would hurt economic activity without improving financial stability." (FY2023 letter). CET1 requirement 11.4% in 2026 vs 10.9% expected in 2025 at the same 3.4% SCB, unexplained A
H5 Conduct and reputation (1MDB) $3.42bn 2020 litigation provisions; Malaysia $2.5bn plus a ≥$1.4bn recovery guarantee; ~$174m clawbacks A
H6 Private-credit stress, 2026 Bantwal: "But the reality is that it's not semiliquid, it's illiquid." (Mar 23 2026). Blostein: "evergreen retail funds in private credit will remain in net outflows throughout 2026 and likely 2027". Software ~25% of direct lending A, framed as technical. I: GS sits on both the origination (CSG) and investing (GSAM) sides, an allocation conflict nobody discusses
H7 AI execution "Changing processes in a big enterprise is hard work." (Solomon, Jan 23 2026). Covello's "six times the cost". Churchman on junior-pipeline "cognitive atrophy" (Aug 24 2026) A. I: gains competed away across banks
H8 Operational and automation risk; cyber Varadhan: "so much of our workflow has migrated through technological automation" (Nov 21 2023). Solomon on cyber: "It's something I've worried about for a long time." (Feb 24 2023) A
H9 Geopolitics and fiscal US–China two-sphere world (Solomon, 2019); Brexit (~6,000 UK staff, 2019); Iran (FY2025 letter); Waldron: "the bond market is starting to be heard" (Jun 5 2025) A
H10 Talent competition with Big Tech and non-banks Senior engineering hires from AWS, Google (twice) and Amazon AGI (2019–26); Bellevue office near the Amazon and Microsoft campuses (Sep 2026); Solomon would hire more engineers "if we weren't constrained by our desire to drive returns" (paraphrase; see goldman ai) I
H11 Opaque platform economics Marquee: no users, revenue or pricing disclosed anywhere (2014–2026) I
H12 Moving goalposts Alts target switched from $100bn net inflows (FY2019 letter) to $150bn gross (FY2020). The top-client metric moved from top-100 to top-150 with a restated base. "Through the cycle" returns language arrived once 2022–23 ROE fell short I

What Goldman acknowledges vs leaves out: it openly discusses cyclicality, consumer losses (briefly), capital rules, 1MDB, AI execution and cyber. It does not discuss rival dealers, venue consolidation (ICE–MarketAxess, Tradeweb–Trumid), its share of electronic flow after 2020, Marquee economics, or the originator-versus-investor conflict in private credit.

4. Five forces from a dealer's seat, 2026

Pressure score: 1 = benign, 5 = severe (judgement). Arrows show change since 2019. GS's channels barely name rivals, so venue and NBLP evidence leans on the Tradeweb study, cited.

Force Score Trend Evidence Read (inference)
Venues (Tradeweb, MarketAxess/ICE, CME) 3 ↑ GS's own electronic share of tickets in 2019: ~75% of US credit, ~99.9% of US cash equities (ID20). Portfolio trading "$120bn+ executed since inception" (ID20 slide). GS proposes a TRACE tweak that "could improve execution quality in even the most illiquid bonds" (undated credit-PT article). Dealers' stake in Tradeweb fell from 46% to 17.3% at the 2019 IPO (tradeweb strategy financials). ICE agreed to buy MarketAxess (Jul 30 2026) and Tradeweb to buy Trumid (Oct 19 2026, GS advising Trumid). None of this appears on GS's channels Venues commoditise the flow spread and are consolidating into stacks with data and clearing. GS's answer is to be a venue too (Sigma X ATS/MTF), to own pre-trade (Marquee), and to grow where venues can't follow: financing. Electronic stats appear in 2020 and never again in the letters
Non-bank liquidity providers (Citadel Securities, Jane Street) 4 ↑ Host Mahajan to Griffin: Citadel Securities has "double digit market share" in equities, futures and treasuries (Jul 9 2026). Griffin: large market makers spend "hundreds of millions of dollars on compute". Jeria on retail flow internalized off-exchange: "non-participable" (Jun 2022). Jane Street is never named The sharpest rival for intermediation share. Compute as a fixed cost favours the largest, which includes GS, but GS's edge is balance sheet and client wallet, not speed. NBLPs are also prime-brokerage clients
Private-credit funds (Apollo, Ares, Blackstone, Oaktree) 3 ↑ Rowan: "So, who are the new banks? Investors." (Feb 10 2023). GS alts fundraising 2020–22 trailed Blackstone, Apollo, KKR and Brookfield (ID23 peer table). Pete Lyon: "I think we're in the middle of a market structure change." (Jun 8 2026) Double-edged. They take loans dealers once held, and they are GBM's financing clients and GSAM's competitors. Capital Solutions is GS's bid to originate for them. The 2026 stress tests both sides at once
Big Tech (Apple, AWS, Google, model labs) 3 ↑ Apple chose GS because "we had no legacy business" (Solomon, Oct 1 2019), then moved the card to Chase (Jan 7 2026). AWS: cloud partner and source of the CIO. Argenti: "those who own the models will own the new operating systems that power AI agents." (Jan 22 2026) Big Tech holds distribution (Apple) and the platform layer (cloud, models). It took the customer relationship in consumer and could take the interface in institutional workflow. It is also GS's biggest AI-debt issuer client
Regulators (Fed, SEC, CFTC, EU, PRA) 3 (was 4) ↓ since 2025 SCB 6.7% → 3.4%; Basel III endgame fight; 1MDB. Then Jul 1 2025: "A more balanced approach to the tests would allow Goldman Sachs to continue to serve our clients’ needs" The single biggest swing factor in returns: every 100bp of SCB is capital that can't be bought back. Relief is political and can reverse
Buyer power (asset managers, sponsors, corporates) 3 → The CCP paper allied GS with BlackRock, Vanguard and JPM; wallet share +390bp; QIA's $25bn came with a Doha commitment Big clients multi-home across dealers. GS competes on rank, not price
Supplier power (talent, compute, data vendors) 3 ↑ 12,000 engineers; Big Tech hires; MarketView redistributes LSEG, FactSet, MSCI, Axioma and Wolfe data (Nov 2023) Talent and compute are bid up by the same AI boom GS finances

Read: the forces that compress the flow business (venues, NBLPs) are rising. Goldman's response has been to move its growth to where those forces are weak: balance-sheet financing, alternatives fees and advice. The forces that matter most for those businesses are the regulator (capital) and the private-credit funds (competitors and clients). That is why the 2024 SCB dispute and the 2026 private-credit stress mattered more to the firm than any venue merger. Contrast Tradeweb, for which the venue mergers are the main threat (tradeweb mission forces §4).

5. Crisis tests — what each revealed

Shock What Goldman said Numbers (as stated) What it revealed (inference)
COVID, Mar–Jun 2020 Solomon to staff (Mar 1 2020): "We have managed through volatile markets before – it’s core to what we do." Buybacks paused Mar 16; Fed discount window used Mar 17. FY2020 letter on critics who wanted Global Markets shrunk: "wise to stay the course" Q1 2020 GM return 19.7% vs 11% threshold; Q2 2020 FICC $4.24bn, "its highest quarterly performance in nine years", and Equities $2.94bn (+46%); first SCB 6.7% (Jun 29), cut to 6.6% after the Fed's error; $2.01bn of 1MDB provisions in the same quarter Volatility is revenue. The trading franchise the 2020 plan meant to dilute carried the year. The consumer program offered payment holidays; it was a cost, not a cushion
2022 drawdown (Ukraine, rates, equity issuance near a two-decade low) "It was a turbulent quarter dominated by the devastating invasion of Ukraine." (Apr 14 2022). Q4 2022 "an outlier quarter" (Feb 24 2023) FY2022 ROE 10.2% vs 23.0%; FICC $14.68bn (+38%); ~$10bn negative swing on the AM balance sheet; Russia markdown; realignment announced Oct 18 2022 Markets held, the balance sheet and consumer didn't. The crisis produced the strategic retreat: narrowed consumer, the client-capital AWM model, and the "exceptional" purpose
SVB / regional banks, Mar 2023 "The events of the first quarter acted as another real-life stress test" (Apr 18 2023). SVB is never named in the corpus Q1 2023 ROE 11.6%; FICC −17% YoY; record Equities financing; Marcus loan sale loss ~$470m booked the same quarter GS framed itself with "the nation’s largest financial institutions" against the regionals. The consumer unwind accelerated in the same quarter. GS Research later called private credit "a very solid line of defense against the risk of a credit crunch" in that episode (Karoui, Apr 15 2025)
Tariffs, Apr 2025 "in times of great uncertainty, clients turn to Goldman Sachs for execution and insight" (Apr 14 2025). Waldron: "We have moderated our risk positioning since April 2nd." (Jun 5 2025) Q1 2025 Equities $4.19bn, a record including record financing; ROE 16.9% (Q1) then 12.8% (Q2); Equities $4.30bn (+36%) in Q2; capital-markets deals paused, then "10 or so IPOs" priced by late May Financing plus prime held while the advisory pipeline stalled. The firm cut risk rather than lean in, consistent with the durability pitch
Private-credit stress, Mar–May 2026 (plus the Iran conflict) Bantwal: not semiliquid but illiquid; Lynam: limits are "a feature, not a bug"; Brandmeyer: "So, the system is gummed up. The circulatory system is not working." (Jun 8 2026) Retail redemptions ~10% unannualized in Q1 (Mar 23 2026); alt-manager stocks −30–40% (Blostein); yet Q1 2026 ROE 19.8%, Q2 2026 revenue $20.34bn and ROE 23.5% (records), Equities $7.42bn GBM profits from the volatility while AWM carries the stress. Goldman is long the theme on both sides. The house line (not systemic) held through Q3 2026 (ROE 18.7%, "second highest quarterly net revenues")

Pattern: each shock confirmed that the trading-and-financing franchise is the shock absorber and that the businesses meant to diversify away from it (consumer, balance-sheet investing) were the ones that broke. The blind spot: Goldman reports how it performed in each crisis, never how a client fared on its platform or its products. That is the outside-voices gap (goldman outside voices §9).

7. Canon lenses

  • Purpose as narrative (canon sinek start with why): Goldman's why changed four times in seven years. A why that follows the what is a positioning statement, not a purpose. Test it against the Whitehead principles, which didn't change.
  • Culture (canon schein organizational culture): the artifacts (purpose boxes, boilerplate) moved fast; the espoused values (four core values) didn't; the basic assumptions (client first, risk discipline, apprenticeship) show up in crises and in 1MDB's fixes.
  • Industry structure (canon porter competitive strategy): §4. From a dealer's seat, the flow business faces rising rivalry and substitutes. The financing business faces mainly the regulator.
  • Powers (canon helmer 7 powers): GS's durable power is scale economies in balance sheet and risk plus a cornered resource in senior client relationships. Network effects belong to the venues, not the dealer.
  • Disruption (canon christensen innovators dilemma): consumer was GS trying to be the disruptor and failing on distribution economics. NBLPs and private credit are disrupting GS from below in intermediation and lending.
  • Antifragile and fragile parts (canon taleb antifragile): trading gains from disorder; balance-sheet investing and consumer credit were fragile to it. The 2020–25 strategy cut the fragile parts.
  • Luck vs skill (canon mauboussin success equation): separate volatility-driven quarters from the financing and fee build before crediting the strategy.
  • Good strategy (canon rumelt good strategy): the Investor Day 2020 plan had a diagnosis (too volatile, too capital-heavy), but its guiding policy (diversify into consumer) was the wrong one. The coherent action that worked was the one it didn't headline: financing.

Part 1 — compute the financing shift, then stress it. Use the release figures:

FICC intermediation FICC financing Equities intermediation Equities financing
FY2022 $11.89bn $2.79bn $6.66bn $4.33bn
FY2025 $10.27bn $4.25bn $9.34bn $7.20bn
  1. Financing share of FICC + Equities revenue in each year. Answer: 2022: (2.79 + 4.33) / 25.67 = 27.7%. 2025: (4.25 + 7.20) / 31.06 = 36.9% (derived).
  2. Growth 2022 → 2025 of financing vs intermediation. Answer: financing 7.12 → 11.45, +61%. Intermediation 18.55 → 19.61, +6% (derived).
  3. A calm year: intermediation falls 30% from 2025 and financing is flat. New total and financing share? Answer: intermediation 19.61 × 0.7 = 13.73; total 13.73 + 11.45 = $25.18bn, down 18.9%; financing share 45.5% (derived). Compare Waldron's 6% standard deviation claim: one calm year at this size would be roughly a three-sigma event on his measure. Either his window is unrepresentative or calm years are rarer than they used to be.

Part 2 — Rumelt's kernel for Goldman 2027 in ≤120 words. One possible answer: - Diagnosis: flow intermediation is being commoditised by venues and non-bank market makers. Goldman's returns now rest on balance-sheet financing and alternatives fees, and the regulator prices that balance sheet. - Guiding policy: be the client's balance sheet and capital-markets adviser, not its cheapest executor. Grow fee-paying alternatives without becoming a forced seller of its own clients' risk. - Coherent actions: (1) publish financing and AWM durability metrics every quarter; (2) separate CSG origination from GSAM allocation with an independent allocation committee; (3) keep electronic execution at par through venues and Marquee, not proprietary bets; (4) treat the SCB as a product constraint in every new business case.

Test: which headwind (H1–H12) does no action touch? (Hint: H5 conduct and H10 talent.) Then check the Q4 2026 release (Jan 2027) for the financing share.
